q: Put the levels of organization in order, from the smallest and simplest to the largest and most complex.
Fill in the missing level: chemical level → cell → ____ → organ → organ system → organism.
Which statement best describes the difference between anatomy and physiology?
options: Anatomy studies structures; physiology studies how they work
Anatomy studies organs; physiology studies cells
Anatomy studies healthy bodies; physiology studies disease
Anatomy studies the whole body; physiology studies one system

q: A student measures how fast the heart's chambers fill with blood between beats. Which field is the student working in?
A surgeon preparing for a hand operation reviews every bone, muscle, joint and blood vessel in the hand together. Which approach to anatomy is this?
The wall of the urinary bladder contains a lining, layers of muscle, and supporting tissue with blood vessels running through it. At which level of organization is the bladder?
Select all the organs that belong to the digestive system.
Select all the organs that belong to more than one organ system.
What defines a vessel as an artery?
options: It carries blood high in oxygen
It carries blood away from the heart
Its wall is a single layer of cells
It carries blood back to the heart
misconception: arteries are defined by carrying oxygenated blood

q: Oxygen passes from the blood to the cells of your calf muscle. In which vessels does most of this exchange happen?
You touch a hot pan and pull your hand away before you think about it. Which characteristic of life does this show most directly?
What does the term metabolism mean?
options: All the chemical changes in the body
The breakdown of food inside the stomach
The rate at which the heart beats
The increase in the number of cells

q: This description of the levels of organization has one wrong step. Find it.
options: Several organs combine to form a tissue.
Organs that share a job form an organ system.
Organ systems together make the organism.

q: On a cold day your skin cools, you start shivering, with small, rapid muscle contractions that make heat, and your body temperature stays near 37 °C. What does this show?
options: The body keeps an internal condition within a normal range
Muscles work only in cold weather
The outside temperature sets the temperature inside your body

q: You travel from sea level to a town high in the mountains. Predict each change on your first day there.

variables.name: Pressure of the air around you
Oxygen entering your blood with each breath
Number of organ systems in your body

q: Mr. Okafor's kidneys have almost stopped working. Water builds up in his blood, his ankles swell, and fluid collects in his lungs. Which chain best explains why he is now short of breath?
options: Fluid builds up, collects in his lungs and cuts oxygen entry
Urinary failure directly damages the airway, so air cannot reach his lungs
His lungs have failed first, which then caused his kidneys to fail
Swollen ankles press on the lungs from below and stop them expanding

q: Which organ system includes the thymus and the spleen?
Which structure carries urine from the urinary bladder out of the body?
In the term gastritis, which part is the word root?
What is a combining form?
options: A prefix and a suffix joined without a root
Two roots joined without any vowel
A word root plus a linking vowel, such as cardi/o
A suffix that turns a noun into an adjective

q: A patient's chart says hepatomegaly. What does the term mean?
A surgeon removes a patient's kidney. Which term names the procedure?
A patient is breathing 8 times a minute, far slower than normal. Which term describes this?
Select every term that contains a prefix.
Put the steps for decoding an unfamiliar medical term in order.
options: Read the suffix to learn what kind of word it is
Read the prefix, if there is one, to learn how the meaning is modified
Read the root or roots to learn which body part it is about
Combine the parts, starting from the suffix
Check the literal meaning against the definition

q: Which spelling correctly joins gastr/o and -itis?
Build the term for the study of the stomach and intestines: gastr + ____ + enter + o + logy.
A student builds the term for an inflamed stomach. One step is wrong. Find it.
options: Choose the root for stomach: gastr
Keep the o, since -itis begins with a vowel
Join the parts to make a single word

q: A 29-year-old woman tells the triage nurse that it burns when she passes urine. The nurse writes a single term in the chart for this symptom. Which term fits?
Renal and nephrectomy both refer to the kidney, yet they use different roots. What explains this?
options: They refer to different parts of the kidney
One root is Latin and the other is Greek
Renal describes disease, and nephr describes healthy tissue
Nephr is a prefix and ren is a root

q: Select every suffix that names a procedure rather than a condition.
Build the term for an enlarged spleen.
A medicine is given by subcutaneous injection. Where does the needle deliver it?
options: Between one rib and the next

q: The word artery comes from a Greek word for an air duct. What does this example show about decoding?
options: Arteries carry air as well as blood
Greek roots are less accurate than the Latin roots
Literal meanings still need checking against the definition
Only terms with a prefix can be decoded

q: In the anatomical position, which way do the palms face?
A patient is lying flat on their back, face up. What is this position called?
Which term means closer to the midline of the body?
In the anatomical position, how is the thumb described relative to the little finger?
Which statement uses proximal correctly?
options: The wrist is proximal to the elbow
The ankle is proximal to the knee
The elbow is proximal to the wrist
The fingers are proximal to the palm

q: Where does the breastbone lie relative to the heart?
Select every pair of terms that mean the same direction in a standing human.
Which statement uses superficial or deep correctly?
options: Bone is superficial to muscle in the thigh
The skin is deep to the fat under it
Muscle is deep to the skin
The skin is deep to the bone

q: A 71-year-old man has a stroke that damages the right side of his brain. Most pathways between the brain and the body cross the midline. Where would you expect weakness?
options: In the right arm and leg
In the left arm and leg
In the face only, on the right

q: Your right arm and right leg are on the same side of the body. Which term describes them?
A patient lies supine on a stretcher. Which statement about her is correct?
options: Her chest is now superior because it faces the ceiling
Her face is still anterior to her ears
Her feet are now posterior to her knees
Her back is now inferior to her chest
misconception: directional terms change with body position

q: The nose is medial to the eye, and the ear is lateral to it. How is the eye described relative to the nose and ear?
A student raises an arm straight overhead and says, "Now my hand is superior to my elbow, so it is proximal." What is the error?
options: The hand is still distal to the elbow in every posture
The hand becomes proximal only when the elbow is bent
Proximal and distal are used only on the trunk
The hand is lateral, not proximal

q: Here is a description of the anatomical position. One item is wrong. Find it.
options: The body stands upright, facing forward.
The feet are flat on the floor and point forward.
The arms hang at the sides.
The palms face the thighs, with the thumbs forward.

q: An EMT reports "a laceration on the lateral left forearm, just proximal to the wrist." Where is the wound?
options: On the thumb side of the left forearm, a little toward the elbow from the wrist
On the little-finger side of the left forearm, just below the elbow
On the thumb side of the right forearm, on the back of the hand
On the little-finger side of the left forearm, toward the fingers from the wrist

q: Put these structures of the upper limb in order from most proximal to most distal.
Complete the pairs of opposites: superior ↔ inferior; anterior ↔ posterior; medial ↔ lateral; superficial ↔ ____.
Which plane divides the body into right and left parts?
Which plane divides the body into anterior and posterior parts?
A section cuts through the right eye and the part of the brain directly behind it. It misses the nose and the left eye. Which plane made it?
What is another name for the frontal plane?
A pathologist sees a round ring of tissue with a hollow center under the microscope. What is the most likely explanation?
options: A tube cut in cross section
A tube cut in longitudinal section
A solid ball cut through its middle
A flat sheet cut at a slant

q: Select every term that names the transverse plane or its cut.
What is the difference between a plane and a section?
options: A plane is horizontal; a section is vertical
A plane is an imaginary surface; a section is the cut it produces
A plane is used for single organs; a section is used for the whole body
A plane is seen on a scan; a section is seen only in dissection

q: A pregnant patient needs imaging of her gallbladder, and her doctor wants to avoid ionizing radiation. Which method fits best?
On a radiograph of the forearm, the bones look white and the surrounding soft tissue looks gray. What causes this difference?
options: Bone reflects sound waves back toward the probe on the skin
Bone gives off radio signals in a magnetic field
Bone absorbs more of the X-rays passing through it
Bone takes up more of an injected tracer

q: Put the steps of making a CT image in order.
options: An X-ray source spins around the patient, sending beams through from many angles
Detectors record how much each beam was weakened
A computer calculates the density at every point in a thin slice
The densities are shown as shades from black to white in a transverse section
The stack of transverse sections is rebuilt into sagittal or frontal views

q: On a chest radiograph, a coin in the patient's shirt pocket appears on top of the heart shadow. Why can't the radiograph alone tell whether the coin is in front of or behind the heart?
options: A coin is too small and too faint to show clearly on a radiograph
Radiographs flatten everything on a beam's path into one image
misconception: a plain X-ray shows a slice

q: A radiologist reads a transverse CT slice of a patient's abdomen. The liver appears on the left side of the screen. On which side of the patient is the liver?
options: It cannot be known from a CT slice
It depends on whether the patient was prone

q: A patient with a metal fragment near the eye needs imaging. Which method is most likely to be unsafe?
A doctor wants to see which areas of a patient's body contain very active cells, such as an active cancer. Which method shows this best?
Complete the list. Sagittal divides right from left; frontal divides anterior from posterior; transverse divides ____.
A student lists how each imaging method works. One entry is wrong. Find it.
options: Radiograph: X-rays absorbed by dense tissue leave white areas on a flat image
CT: X-rays from many angles are turned into sections by a computer
MRI: X-rays and a radioactive tracer make sections in any plane
Ultrasound: echoes of sound waves make a live section

q: Which cavity holds the brain?
Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
Select every structure that lies in the mediastinum.
A 22-year-old man is stabbed just to the left of his breastbone, and the blade reaches his heart. Which compartment of the thoracic cavity contains the organ the blade reached?
Which layer of a serous membrane lines the wall of the cavity?
A student says, "The right lung sits inside the right pleural cavity." Where does the right lung actually lie?
options: Inside the pleural cavity, floating in serous fluid
In the thoracic cavity, but outside the pleural cavity
In the mediastinum, with the pleural cavity below it
In the abdominopelvic cavity, just above the diaphragm
misconception: organs sit inside their serous cavity

q: Put these spaces in order from the largest, which contains the others, to the smallest.
Complete the statement. The dorsal body cavity = the cranial cavity + the ____.
Ms. Reyes, 34, has a sharp pain on the right side of her chest each time she breathes in. Her doctor hears a grating sound over that area with every breath. What best explains the pain and the sound?
options: Fluid has leaked into her vertebral canal
Her lung has slipped into the pericardial cavity
The pleural layers are rough and rubbing
Her diaphragm has separated the two pleural cavities

q: A surgeon opens the front wall of the abdomen to reach the stomach. Which serous membrane must the surgeon pass through?
options: The serous membrane around the heart
The protective layers around the brain

q: In which cavity does an empty urinary bladder lie?
A needle is passed through the chest wall to drain extra fluid from around a lung. A student lists what it passes through, from outside in. One step is wrong. Find it.
options: Skin and the fat beneath it

q: Fluid builds up in a patient's pericardial cavity faster than it is removed. Predict each change.

variables.name: Space between the two serous layers around the heart
How fully the heart can fill between beats
Number of layers in the serous membrane

q: A cyclist hits the handlebars and tears her spleen. The spleen bleeds into the serous space around it. Where does the blood collect?
What does the film of serous fluid between the two layers of a serous membrane do?
options: It carries oxygen to the organ
It lets the layers slide with little friction
It forms a hard shell that shields the organ
It glues the organ to the backbone

q: Select every organ that lies in the abdominopelvic cavity.
A wound lets air into a patient's right pleural cavity, and the right lung collapses. The left lung keeps working. What explains this?
options: Each lung has its own separate pleural cavity
The diaphragm seals the left lung off inside the abdomen
Air cannot enter a pleural cavity from outside
The left lung sits in the dorsal body cavity

q: What is the serosa of the stomach?
options: The layer lining the abdominal wall
The fluid in the peritoneal cavity
The visceral layer covering the stomach
The muscle that churns the stomach

q: When the diaphragm contracts, what happens to the thoracic cavity?
options: It merges with the abdominal cavity

q: In anatomical terms, what does the leg (the crural region) include?
options: The whole lower limb, from hip to toes
Only the part from the hip to the knee
Only the part from the knee to the ankle
misconception: the leg is the whole lower limb

q: Which regional term refers to the neck?
A phlebotomist draws blood from a vein at the front of the elbow, in the crease where the elbow bends. Which region is this?
Select every term that names a region of the upper limb.
Which two planes form the lines that divide the abdomen into four quadrants?
options: Midsagittal and transverse, crossing at the navel
Two parasagittal planes and two transverse planes
A frontal plane and a transverse plane

q: Jordan, 19, has pain that began around his navel and has moved low on his right side. It is sharp when he coughs. Which quadrant should the nurse record?
A patient has tenderness in the left upper quadrant after a fall onto her left side. Which organ is most likely injured?
Put the three regions of the middle column of the nine-region grid in order, from top to bottom.
Which abdominopelvic region lies over the stomach, in the upper middle of the abdomen?
Complete the top row of the nine-region grid, from the patient's right to left: right hypochondriac, ____, left hypochondriac.
A student describes how to draw the four abdominal quadrants. One step is wrong. Find it.
options: Picture the patient in the anatomical position
Draw a vertical line down the midline
Draw a horizontal line through the navel
Name each quadrant by the viewer's right and left

q: Early in appendicitis, pain is often felt around the navel even though the appendix lies low on the right. What explains this?
options: The appendix lies in the umbilical region at first
Organ-wall pain is vague and felt near the midline
The navel is where the four quadrant lines cross
The appendix moves from the left to the right side

q: Which regional term refers to the thigh?
Select every pair that correctly matches a region with the part of the body it names.
A clinician wants to place a patient's pain more exactly than a quadrant allows. Which system should she use?
options: The dorsal and ventral body cavities

q: In the nine-region grid, which region holds the appendix?
A paramedic reports a deep cut "in the left popliteal region." Where is the wound?
options: At the front of the left elbow
On the sole of the left foot

q: In the nine-region grid, which region lies directly below the right hypochondriac region?
